text.content: Centered on Marquette University's campus and extending north past Mount Sinai Medical Center, west to the Children's Hospital of Wisconsin, and south nearly to the Menomonee River, this area is saturated with magic so dense that Thaumaturgical rituals fail within it and any Path power risks aggravated backlash on a botch. Auspex, by contrast, operates unusually well here, though a botch while using it can leave the user detectably "marked" to Lupines. Protean is quietly more potent here too, activating some of its powers (Gleam of Red Eyes, Wolf's Claws) almost of its own accord and waiving the normal blood cost for transformations — a fact the investigating @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} have not yet discovered. At the heart of the disturbance lie two Garou totem fragments (the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote) that the renegade Lupine Usla stole and buried here before his death; whoever recovers them gains potent (and dangerous) power, and the eternal enmity of every Lupine. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Dr. Mortius has studied the zone for decades from a haunted house near the campus, using the unwitting occultists of the Church of Isis at Mount Mary College as pawns.

The Milwaukee Exposition and Convention Center and Arena (MECCA), linked by an enclosed sky-walk to the Hyatt Regency, the Auditorium and Arena, and the H. Reuss Federal Plaza, is the seat of Kindred power in West-Downtown. The Council of Elders meets here regularly, several Elders (including Lucina) keep permanent rooms in the Hyatt, and a Dominated ghoul karate champion named Raoul commands a heavily armed mortal security detail that keeps Anarchs from getting past the lobby. Symphony performances at the Auditorium double as a favored venue for Council negotiations, since the music covers whispered conversations between votes.

West-Downtown's central Kindred hunting ground, known to the Cainites of Milwaukee as the Crucible, encompasses a cluster of bars and dance clubs — Missing Persons, Arabian Nights, Deadman's Party, Peaches and Cream, Soldier Boy, Howler, and Starscape — each catering to a different slice of Milwaukee's mortal and immortal nightlife. No single faction controls the Crucible, making it one of the few places in the city where Anarchs and Elders hunt within sight of one another without incident.

Where I-94 meets I-794 and I-45 in a snarl of on- and off-ramps, small concrete courtyards abandoned by the world beneath the overpasses have become the preferred battleground for the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers} and the Union. Rarely patrolled by police and too awkward for the homeless to easily occupy, the Interchange sees more Anarch bloodshed than anywhere else in Milwaukee.

pages.name: Good Hope Road and the Outlands Border

text.content: Marking the northern edge of Kindred-controlled territory before the Outlands and Lupine territory beyond, Good Hope Road is patrolled by Mark Decker and the Anubi. Anarchs dare one another to drive its length as a rite of courage — "Doing Good Hope" — and those who survive it five times call themselves Aces. Graceland Cemetery just to the south is one of Milwaukee's traditional dueling grounds, once favored by Elders and now claimed by Anarchs.

Turk and the East Side Anarchs Union make their haven aboard a derelict, banner-hung riverboat run aground along the coast of Veterans Park, a location Turk favors for its resistance to fire — a danger he fears abnormally. The park's homeless population serves as a ready-made herd for the Union, and the parks stretching along the lakeshore have become an infiltration route for Lupines swimming in from the north or south.

pages.name: Old St. Mary's Church (Society of Leopold Cell)

text.content: Beneath an unremarkable East Downtown cathedral, the Society of Leopold maintains a secret basement cell where its members compile what they have learned about Milwaukee's Vampires and Werewolves. Former Prince Merik's standing policy — upheld out of fear that provoking the Inquisition could bring worse attention — is to leave the Society alone and hope it finds nothing worth acting on.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers}' favored after-hours hangout, courtesy of a Dominated security guard who lets them walk in the front gate. The brewery's fermentation-stage aromas and the gang's own smuggled-in music and lighting make for raucous, semi-regular parties deep into the fermenting rooms.
